transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Ruth Park (Mapleaf), James O'Leary (Mapleaf), Priya Narang (Mapleaf), Samir Kaur (Mapleaf)

Optional auto sections (auto-generated):
Summary: Align on exact go/no-go thresholds for POC, how we'll measure them, and what reports look like. Agree who runs what and by when.
Topics: success criteria; workload sizing (QPS, tokens); bench harness and tolerance; reporting and run cadence.
Action items (auto): see action_items field.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. do we have audio okay?
[00:12] Ruth (Mapleaf): yep good here, thanks Alex.
[00:15] Alex: cool. main goal for today is to lock the acceptance rubric — like specifically what constitutes go vs no-go for the poc. speed, accuracy, and cost basically. also confirm who owns the runs.
[00:28] James (Mapleaf): sounds good. to give context, our most common path is the symptom extraction pipeline, average request is roughly 120 tokens in, 40 tokens out. concurrency peaks around 120 qps across our batch workers but single-request latency still matters for UI flow.
[00:45] Diego (Redwood SE): ok so two buckets — batch style embedding/async and low-latency interactive calls. we should size both. for interactive we look at p50/p90/p99 latency and for bulk we look at throughput and cost per 1M tokens.
[01:05] Priya (Mapleaf): correct. our target SLA is 99.9% availability for the inference endpoint and sub-400ms p90 for interactive ideally. that's what PMs will want to see.
[01:18] Alex: noted, 99.9% avail and 400ms p90. quick note though — on smaller GPU stacks p99 can spike, we typically set go/no-go on p90 and a p99 guardrail. is customer okay with p90 primary?
[01:34] Ruth: yes p90 primary is fine, but we want to see p99 numbers and a runbook for fallback behavior.
[01:41] Diego: we'll include automatic fallback policies in the runbook — e.g., route to a cheaper variant or queue with graceful degradation. also note kv cache behavior for chat sessions can reduce tokens — was the plan to test with fresh sessions or warm cache?
[01:56] Samir (Mapleaf): both. 60% of our traffic is returning users with warm contexts, 40% are cold. so please include both patterns.
[02:06] Alex: perfect. let's talk metrics: what accuracy/regression thresholds do you want on the symptom extraction NLU model?
[02:15] James: for the extraction we have two metrics — exact slot F1 and semantic similarity on free-text suggestions. F1 we need at least 0.88 on the representative set, and semantic similarity (cosine) at 0.85 min. If either drops more than 3% vs baseline we consider it a fail.
[02:36] Diego: ok 0.88 F1 and 0.85 sim. for hallucination/failure rate, what tolerance?
[02:42] Ruth: less than 2% critical hallucinations on our 2k test set. anything above that means no-go.
[02:49] Alex: got it. on cost — do you have a target budget per 1k tokens or per month?
[02:54] James: we modeled: limit is $0.03 per 1k tokens on average across mixed workload. if benchmark shows >$0.04 we need to revisit quantization or Dedicated sizing.
[03:06] Diego: we'll report cost both as nominal $/1k tokens and an extrapolated monthly spend for your traffic profile.
[03:13] Priya: what about concurrency tests? we need a synthetic run at 150 concurrent steady-state for 30 minutes and a spike test to 300 for 5 minutes to validate autoscaling/burst.
[03:26] Alex: makes sense. we'll plan one steady 30m and one spike. Diego will coordinate the Dedicated capacity window.
[03:33] Diego: quick note on infra: for network we need VPC peering and egress rules; Priya I assume you've got the network ticket?
[03:40] Priya: yes we'll open the peering on Monday; I can confirm the maintenance window by EOD Friday.
[03:47] Samir: also, please ensure the harness can replay user sequences with KV cache enabled — as Diego mentioned, it's critical for performance.
[03:54] Diego: yes, harness supports warm/cold cache modes. we'll capture token counts, batch sizes, p50/p90/p99, QPS, and GPU utilization.
[04:03] Alex: reporting format — Ruth, James, what do you prefer? we can do a CSV export plus a live Redwood dashboard link.
[04:10] Ruth: csv with columns is necessary for our analytics team, plus a simple summary pdf. the columns we need: timestamp, request_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, node_id, error_flag, f1_score(optional), semantic_score(optional).
[04:26] Alex: noted. we'll attach the sample schema after the call. we'll also put an aggregated sheet with p50/p90/p99 and cost breakdown per model variant.
[04:36] James: one more thing around sample size — you mentioned 2k prompt set. can you confirm distribution? we want at least 30% long-context (>300 tokens) and the rest split across short/medium.
[04:48] Samir: yes, distribution will be 30% long, 50% medium (80-200 tokens), 20% short (<80). We'll provide labels where possible.
[04:58] Diego: for the acceptance tests we'll run: 1) Functional correctness suite (2k labeled), 2) Latency & throughput treadmill (steady and spike), 3) Cost simulation ramp, 4) Regression detector comparing baseline to POC model.
[05:12] Ruth: how do we define regression detector? a simple statistical delta on F1 with bootstrapped CI?
[05:18] Diego: yes we use bootstrap to get CI; default fail rule is delta > 3% and lower CI does not overlap baseline. we'll include the exact test script in the runbook.
[05:28] Alex: let's capture the exact go/no-go thresholds on the call so there's no ambiguity. I'll read back what I have and you confirm.
[05:35] Alex: go if: 1) interactive p90 <= 400ms; 2) availability >= 99.9%; 3) extraction F1 >= 0.88 and semantic sim >= 0.85; 4) hallucinations < 2%; 5) cost <= $0.03 per 1k tokens (extrapolated); and 6) concurrency tests pass (steady 150, spike 300). otherwise no-go. Additional guardrail: p99 reported but used for ops planning, not absolute go/fail unless >1s.
[06:02] Ruth: that matches our expectations except for cost — if cost is slightly over but accuracy is better, we might accept a higher cost for a short pilot — say up to $0.035 if agreed.
[06:14] James: agree to a stretch budget of $0.035 for pilot but must be flagged in report.
[06:18] Alex: okay allow a stretch threshold of 0.035 as a flagged pass. we'll mark that in the CSV.
[06:22] Priya: one more ops requirement — we need audit logs per token request for 30 days and SSO-based access to the Redwood dashboard.
[06:30] Diego: Redwood supports audit logs and SAML SSO for the dashboard. we'll provide SOC2 attestation and the security whitepaper link.
[06:37] Ruth: please send the security pack; legal will want encryption in transit and at rest details and KMS integration notes.
[06:45] Alex: will do. we'll drop links: security pack, SOC2, runbook draft, sample CSV, and the benchmark harness repo.
[06:53] Samir: what's the timeline on the benchmark run?
[06:56] Alex: propose we run initial bench next week — Diego you said you can schedule?
[07:00] Diego: yes I can schedule Dedicated-equivalent window on 2026-03-24 or 03-26. prefer 03-26 to give Mapleaf time to gather prompts.
[07:08] Ruth: 03-26 works for us as well.
[07:11] Alex: great. follow-up sync to review results 2026-03-30 10:00 PDT. I'll send invite.
[07:18] James: noted.
[07:20] Diego: small note on measurement noise — we'll run three replicates and report median and IQR.
[07:26] Samir: good, include GPU utilization and batch size histograms so we can tune quantization if needed.
[07:33] Alex: anything else?
[07:36] Priya: please add a short section in the runbook about failure modes and rollback triggers.
[07:40] Alex: will do.
[07:43] Ruth: thanks everyone, this is clear. we'll circulate the prompt set by Tuesday night.
[07:48] Alex: perfect. I'll summarize and send the links + invite. thanks all.
[07:52] (call ends)
